To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the pore network model simulations of the nitrogen sorption data provide the pore size distribution and the pore connectivity and the pore spatial distribution of native and silane-treated porous silica particles.

the pore connectivity of the silanised silica particles is smaller than that of native silica particles and the pore size distribution and spatial distribution of the silanisation process is not uniform.

the pore connectivity and the pore size distribution of the porous chromatographic particles can be determined from nitrogen sorption data and pore network model simulations, and that the pore connectivity can be related to the diffusional resistance within the porous chromatographic particle structure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach to the study of the structure and transport of proteins within porous chromatographic particles.
the evaluation of the porous structure properties of native and silane-modified chromatographic packing particles.
the characterization of the porous structure, the pore connectivity, pore spatial distribution and pore size distribution of the native and silanised silica particles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the deposition of an organosilane layer to the surface of a native silica particle reduces the pore volume, pore diameter and pore spatial distribution, which increases the diffusional transport resistance within the porous particle.
the silanization process of the native silica surface produces a silanization layer that covers the pore surface, thus reducing the pore size and connectivity of the porous structure.

the deposition of a silane layer on the pore surfaces of native silica particles decreases the pore size and the pore connectivity and thus increases the diffusional resistance within the porous silica particles, which is in agreement with the conclusions drawn from the results of the previous studies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the determination of the pore connectivity of a porous particle by nitrogen adsorption isotherm measurements and the pore network model simulations is a useful tool for the evaluation of the diffusion resistance of the porous structure.
the pore connectivity, pore spatial distribution and the pore size distribution can be obtained by matching the experimental sorption data with pore network simulations.

the determination of the pore connectivity of a porous chromatographic particle from nitrogen sorption data and pore network modelling is possible and that the results obtained can be applied in a rational way to the evaluation of mass transfer resistances in chromatographic systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the pore connectivity and the pore size distribution of the porous structures of chromatographic particles can be obtained from nitrogen sorption data using pore network model simulations, and that these parameters are important to understand the diffusional transport of proteins through the porous structure of chromatographic particles.

the pore connectivity and the pore size distribution of the porous structures of the native and silanised silica particles are the main parameters that determine the diffusivity of proteins under unretained condition.

nitrogen sorption measurements can be used to determine the pore connectivity and spatial distribution of the pore network of chromatographic particles, which are key parameters to determine the diffusional properties of proteins within porous structures.
